claim: In the pre-GA v1alpha2 API, InferencePool used fields extensionRef and targetPortNumber, which have since been renamed to endpointPickerRef and targetPorts in the v1 GA spec.
stance_target: the InferencePool field names shown in this April 2025 CNCF post reflect the current (v1 GA) API
scope_conditions: CNCF blog dated April 21 2025, using apiVersion inference.networking.x-k8s.io/v1alpha2 -- superseded by v1 GA inference.networking.k8s.io/v1 seen in other batch sources
quoted_support:
apiVersion: inference.networking.x-k8s.io/v1alpha2
kind: InferencePool
...
spec:
  targetPortNumber: 8000
  selector:
    app: vllm-llama2-7b
  extensionRef:
    name: vllm-llama2-7b-endpoint-picker

claim: The Endpoint Selection Extension (ESE) filter chain for Critical requests checks, in order: queue wait size below 50, then LoRA adapter affinity, then least-queuing, then least-KV-cache, to arrive at a final endpoint.
stance_target: exact scheduling/filter algorithm the endpoint picker runs for latency-critical requests
scope_conditions: CNCF blog worked example, April 2025, describing reference EPP filter logic
quoted_support: The filter flow starts with 'is this a critical request'? If the request is a Critical request, it will then check whether there are LLM endpoints with a wait queue lower than 50... then check whether those endpoints have the LoRA adapter loaded...

claim: For Sheddable (non-critical) requests, the filter requires KV cache utilization below 80% AND fewer than 5 queued requests; if no endpoint meets that bar, the request is dropped (load shed) rather than routed to an overloaded endpoint.
stance_target: GIE implements explicit load-shedding for low-priority requests based on live KV-cache and queue metrics
quoted_support: If the filter sees a request that is Sheddable then it will find LLMs that have lower than 80% KV cache utilization and fewer than 5 requests waiting in its queue. If it cannot find LLM endpoints that meet that criteria, the Sheddable request is dropped.

claim: The Endpoint Selection Extension extracts the modelName from the request body assuming the OpenAI chat completion API format, then matches it against InferenceModel objects' modelName field to resolve backend targets.
stance_target: endpoint selection is driven by parsing an OpenAI-shaped HTTP request body, not by any Kubernetes-native request attribute
scope_conditions: CNCF blog, April 2025, pre-GA InferenceModel CRD (renamed InferenceObjective in v1)
quoted_support: When a request reaches the Endpoint Selection Extension (ESE), it extracts the modelName from the request body. Currently, the ESE expects the request body to follow the OpenAI API format.
